goals: Characterize runoff generation mechanisms (surface vs subsurface) across the Naches watershed's elevation and soil gradients
Validate modeled runoff partitioning against USGS streamflow observations (requires aggregation/routing)
key_processes: Precipitation partitioning (rain vs snow) across elevation gradient
Soil moisture dynamics controlling runoff thresholds

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can resolve local runoff partitioning (QOVER, QDRAI) as a function of elevation-resolved forcing (NLDAS-2) and soil properties. The user has specified three column locations as the exploratory sample.

answerable: Local runoff partitioning (surface vs subsurface) as a function of elevation and soil at the three specified column locations
Snowmelt timing and magnitude across elevation gradient (ELM outputs H2OSNO, QSNOMELT, SNOW)
Soil moisture controls on runoff generation thresholds
Relative contributions of QOVER vs QDRAI across the sample

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation against USGS streamflow gages
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM produces local runoff fluxes (mm/day per column), not integrated streamflow (m³/s at a gage). Comparison requires spatial aggregation and routing from columns to gage outlet.
not_answerable.needs: Runoff aggregation and routing module to convert distributed ELM fluxes to cumulative discharge

not_answerable.aspect: Adequacy of the three user-specified column locations
not_answerable.why: Coordinates provided by user without stratification justification. One coordinate (46.62, -119.90) appears outside the domain bbox (lon -121.5 to -120.5). Cannot verify that the three points span the elevation range (352-1977 m) or soil heterogeneity.
not_answerable.needs: Coordinate validation against domain boundary and DEM/soil sampling to confirm stratification coverage

not_answerable.why: N=3 is a sparse sample for a 1625 m relief watershed. May miss key transitions (rain-snow boundary, soil drainage class shifts, riparian vs upland) if locations are not strategically placed.
not_answerable.needs: Either: (1) verification that user coordinates span key strata, or (2) expanded sampling following stratified design

sampling_strategy.approach: user-specified exploratory sample (3 columns) — intended to span elevation and soil gradients but not verified

bands: mid (900-1500 m) — rain-snow transition, seasonal snowpack

classes: well-drained (sandy loam, loam) — high infiltration, subsurface-dominated runoff
poorly-drained (clay loam, silt loam) — saturation-excess surface runoff

sampling_strategy.n_justification: User-specified sample. Scientifically, N=3 is minimally adequate IF the columns span the elevation bands (low/mid/high) and sample contrasting soil drainage classes. This would isolate elevation (climate/snow) vs soil (infiltration) controls on runoff partitioning. However, without coordinate validation, coverage is unverified.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: INTENDED logic (not verified): one column per elevation band (low/mid/high), sampling both well-drained and poorly-drained soils to contrast infiltration-excess vs saturation-excess runoff generation. Ideally, mid-elevation column targets the rain-snow transition zone (~1200-1400 m) where runoff mechanisms shift seasonally.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — each column represents a unique elevation-soil combination

sampling_plan.reason: Isolate rain-driven runoff with minimal snow influence; test soil infiltration control on QOVER vs QDRAI partitioning
Capture seasonal shift from rain to snowmelt-driven runoff; resolve timing of peak runoff generation
Isolate snowmelt-driven runoff; test delayed runoff response and subsurface drainage from snowmelt infiltration

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — requires spatial aggregation of column fluxes and routing to gage outlet (NOT co-located point comparison)
validation_design.metric: Monthly flow volume bias, seasonal timing correlation, peak flow magnitude RMSE
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on number of USGS gages in HUC 17030002 with sufficient record length (1980-2018)

validation_design.comparison: analog — nearest SNOTEL station to high-elevation column for peak SWE timing and magnitude (expect underestimation due to 12 km forcing averaging over terrain)
validation_design.metric: Peak SWE bias, melt-out date difference
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on SNOTEL station density in Naches watershed

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (1980-2018, full period for climatology), native SSURGO soil at each column location, no spin-up (cold start from default water table)

requires_capabilities.why: To convert distributed ELM column runoff fluxes (mm/day) to cumulative streamflow (m³/s) at USGS gage locations for validation
requires_capabilities.blocks: Direct comparison of modeled runoff to observed streamflow — currently can only compare spatial patterns or analog-site process validation

requires_capabilities.capability: Coordinate validation and DEM/soil sampling at user-specified points
requires_capabilities.why: To verify that the three provided coordinates (1) fall within the domain bbox, (2) span the elevation range, and (3) sample soil heterogeneity as intended
requires_capabilities.blocks: Confirmation that the exploratory sample adequately resolves the drivers — current design assumes coverage but cannot verify

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL station metadata and data ingest for Naches watershed
requires_capabilities.why: To enable snow validation at high-elevation column (peak SWE, melt timing)
requires_capabilities.blocks: Snow process validation — currently can only compare to literature expectations or regional climatology

requires_capabilities.capability: Multi-year spin-up or WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: Cold-start runs initialize all columns at the same default water table (~8.8 m), which may not reflect the real WTD distribution across elevation/soil gradients. This biases initial QDRAI (subsurface drainage) until the aquifer equilibrates.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Accurate representation of subsurface runoff partitioning in early simulation years — recommend either 5+ year spin-up or Fan (2013) WTD-informed initialization

assumptions: The three user-specified coordinates are intended to span the elevation gradient (low/mid/high) and sample contrasting soil drainage classes, though this is not verified.
NLDAS-2 forcing at 0.125° resolution adequately resolves the precipitation and temperature gradients across the 1625 m elevation range (verified for similar basins).

Cold-start initialization (default water table) is acceptable for a runoff generation study focused on surface processes and seasonal snowmelt, though subsurface drainage (QDRAI) will have initialization artifacts in early years.
USGS gage data for HUC 17030002 exists and has sufficient temporal coverage (1980-2018) for validation, though gage locations and record completeness are unknown.
The user's coordinate (46.62, -119.90) is either a typo or the domain bbox is incorrect — this coordinate falls outside the stated western boundary of -120.5 longitude.
